scan_notes: Read the exact origin/develop...HEAD diff, confirmed a clean worktree at bc83c783, and inspected the surrounding resolver, renderer, production builders, shell caller, measurement tool, and tests. Independently verified prior claims (a)-(e) are fixed: every recorded marked trace is checked with the resolver predicate; both exclusion counters are mandatory and checked for no-period-axis; old exclusion-rule records refuse; and both sentence doors derive the projected form from all-projection. The boundary rejects equality and accepts a strictly later latest period. No tests were executed because the filesystem is read-only; runtime conclusions are source-derived inference.

findings.title: Render-time bound failures cannot name the offending trace
findings.evidence: The resolver records only `{"latest": m["latest"], "grain": m["grain"]}` for each projected trace. Consequently, the renderer's refusal at lines 1717-1721 can only say "a marked trace reaches only ..." and cannot identify the trace, despite the stated requirement that it be named.
findings.failure_scenario: A recorded all-projection verdict contains marked traces `collections` ending at the declared edge and `run-off` extending beyond it. `rendered_check_problem` correctly refuses the record, but its error cannot name `collections`, leaving the operator unable to identify which builder trace is mis-marked. Anonymous traces are even less identifiable.
findings.suggested_fix: Record a diagnostic trace label, preferably figure/trace ordinal plus the name when present, in every `projected_traces` entry and include it in the renderer refusal. Do not use that label in the verdict predicate.

findings.title: Sweep still treats period-set movement as settling verdict movement
findings.evidence: The tool sets `row["moved"] = sorted(b) != sorted(c["periods"])` and marks a verdict undecided only when both sets are empty. It later prints that otherwise "the set comparison decides every row", although a changed non-empty period set does not determine whether the resolver verdict changed.
findings.failure_scenario: With declared edge 2026-05, an unmarked actual trace reaches 2026-06 and a neutral-named projection reaches 2026-07. The old module counts both; the current module excludes the marked projection. The period sets differ, but both resolvers refuse because the actual trace still exceeds the edge. The sweep reports movement without flagging the verdict as unmeasured, under a tool described as auditing verdict movement.
findings.suggested_fix: Either resolve the same as-of record through both modules and compare verdict/refusal outcomes, or describe and report only period-set movement and remove the claim that non-empty set comparison settles the verdict.

findings.title: An all-error sweep exits successfully as a zero-movement run
findings.evidence: The dead-probe guard is conditional on `graded`: `if graded and not any(...)`. When every builder was caught as an error, `graded` is empty, the guard is skipped, and execution reaches the normal summary and `return 0`.
findings.failure_scenario: Run the hand measurement against a reachable database lacking every population slot's required tables. Each builder exception is caught into an `error` row, leaving `graded=[]`. The command exits 0 and prints `period set MOVED on 0`, allowing a completely unmeasured run to be treated as successful evidence.
findings.suggested_fix: Exit nonzero when `graded` is empty before applying the existing all-zero dead-probe check.

overall_explanation: The production exclusion mechanism, all-projection boundary, stale-record version gate, and sentence reconstruction are internally consistent on the reviewed paths. The remaining issues are one explicit diagnostic-contract violation at the renderer and two correctness gaps in the hand-run measurement tool; none establishes a production false pass in the current resolver-generated record path.
